question: Is Theorem 117c's necessity strict? Can a non-principal boxt_hat-fixed cut exist in the MacNeille completion WITHOUT a carrier-level Jeroslow point p = boxt p (FP-synt)?
answer: NO, necessity is NOT strict. The self-dual seed is COMPLETION-GENERATED. On the SAME hexagon carrier/order used in Pass 117, and with NO carrier synt-FP, antitone maps that send the lower MacNeille frontier F={x,y} of the unattained middle cut w=xvy=m^n ONTO the upper frontier G={m,n} make w a genuine non-principal boxt_hat-FIXED cut. FP-synt is therefore unnecessary; Thm 117c's clause 'requires ... effectively a Jeroslow FP-synt point' is refuted.

carrier.name: hexagon H
carrier.covers: 0<x, 0<y, x<m, x<n, y<m, y<n, m<U, n<U
carrier.nonprincipal_cut_identity: w = x v y = m ^ n (unique non-principal cut)

general_identity: For any non-principal cut w with lower frontier F=max(w cap L): boxt_hat(w) = /\_{f in F} boxt(f) (antitone De Morgan: image-meet). On the hexagon boxt_hat(w) = boxt x ^ boxt y.
fixed_cut_criterion: w is boxt_hat-fixed  <=>  boxt x ^ boxt y = w = m^n  <=>  {boxt x, boxt y} = G = {m,n}  <=>  boxt[F] = G (lower frontier maps ONTO upper frontier). Parity of the orbit is irrelevant.

witness_A_frontier_cross.orbit_structure: (0 U)(x m y n)  -- a 4-cycle, EVEN
witness_A_frontier_cross.note: boxt[F]={m,n}=G and boxt[G]={x,y}=F (two-way frontier swap, involutive on frontiers)

control_B_pass117_plateau.orbit_structure: (0 U)(x y) with m,n,U -> 0  -- Pass-117 front-internal swap
control_B_pass117_plateau.note: boxt[F]=F (NOT G): boxt_hat(w)= boxt x ^ boxt y = y ^ x = bottom. Reproduces Pass-117 Thm 117a.

hexagon_full_census.scope: ALL antitone boxt on the hexagon with NO carrier synt-FP
hexagon_full_census.conclusion: 22 distinct synt-FP-free antitone maps produce the non-principal fixed cut w; 0 require a carrier fixed point. The 4 two-way frontier swaps (incl. witnesses A,C) are the involutive sub-case.

general_census_small.scope: labelled bounded posets n=4..5, unique bottom/top
general_census_small.remark: Every bounded poset with unique bottom/top on <=5 elements is a lattice (trivial completion). The minimal non-lattice bounded poset is the hexagon (n=6), so the hexagon is the minimal witness carrier.

correction_to_pass117: Thm 117c is split. The Tarski-interval criterion (a fixed cut exists iff [lfp boxt_hat^2, gfp boxt_hat^2] contains a self-dual element) STANDS. The clause identifying the self-dual seed with a carrier-level odd/Jeroslow point p=boxt p is FALSE: the seed can be a NEW cut, realized by an EVEN frontier-swapping orbit with no carrier fixed point.
aps_reading: The MacNeille completion manufactures a phantom self-referential fixed point w (boxt w = w, a Rosser/Henkin-style consistency sentence) that NO base sentence realizes. Fixed-point-level analogue of the earlier phantom-limit passes: completing the Lindenbaum order can introduce self-reference absent downstairs.
verdict: COMPLETION-GENERATED SELF-DUAL SEED CONFIRMED. FP-synt NOT necessary. Operative invariant = boxt[F]=G (frontier-onto), not orbit parity.
